The final answer 2431/50 has the wrong sign. The correct value is −2431/50.

The setup is sound. With g(k) = k²f(k) − 1, g has roots at the eight points n(n+1), so g(k) = c(k − a)p(k), where p(k) = ∏(k − n(n+1)). The conditions g(0) = −1 and g′(0) = 0 are the right ones, and they give a = −9/8. They also give c·a·p(0) = 1 with p(0) = 8!·9!, so c = −8/(9·8!·9!). This is negative, and the solution's c agrees with it.

The error is in the sign of g(90):
- With c < 0, the factor (90 + 9/8) is positive.
- p(90) = ∏(90 − n(n+1)) = 88·84·78·70·60·48·34·18 is positive.
- So g(90) = c(90 + 9/8)p(90) < 0.

Computing it: g(90) = −81·p(90)/(8!·9!) = −81·18!/(10!·9!) = −81·4862 = −393822. The solution reaches the same magnitude, 9·C(18,8) = 393822, but in the middle of its algebra it writes "−9·C(18,8)" and then declares a "sign correction" to +9·C(18,8) with no justification. That flip is unjustified.

Hence f(90) − 1/90² = g(90)/90² = −393822/8100 = −2431/50.

VERDICT: REJECT
